 Versus

Hon'ble Alok Mahra, J.
Mr. Sanjay Kumar Chandel, learned counsel
for the revisionist.
2. Mr. S.C. Dumka, A.G.A. alongwith Mr.
Nikhil Bisht, Brief Holder for the State.
3. This criminal revision has been filed against
the judgment and order dated 02.12.2023 passed
by the court of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Almora in Criminal Complaint Case No. 66 of
2023, Kishan Singh Jeena Vs. Ramesh Singh
Nagarkoti, whereby, the revisionist was convicted
under Section 138 of N.I. Act and sentenced
accordingly. Challenge has also been made to the
judgment and order dated 17.07.2026 passed by
the court of learned Session Judge, Almora in
Criminal Appeal No. 52 of 2023, Ramesh Singh
Nagarkoti Vs. Kishan Singh Jeena and Another,
whereby, the appeal filed by the revisionist
against his conviction was also dismissed.
4. Heard.
5. Admit.
6. Issue notice to respondent no. 2, returnable
within three weeks. Steps to be taken within a
week.
7. Let LCR be summoned.

8. List after LCR is received.
9. Heard on Bail and Suspension of Sentence
Application (IA No.1 of 2026).
10. Learned counsel for the revisionist has
submitted that the complaint was filed on false
and frivolous grounds; that the revisionist had
signed and given the cheques to one Kuldeep
Singh Bisht in the year 2012 itself and later on
Kuldeep Singh Bisht informed the revisionist that
he has destroyed the cheques; that the revisionist
had no knowledge as to how the cheques came
into the hands of the present complainant, who
had presented the said cheques for encashment
before the bank on 26.12.2022 and the cheques
were dishonoured against which the entire
proceedings has been initiated; that the Reserve
Bank of India has issued a circular, whereby, the
policy decision of the RBI was circulated in which
CTS cheques were discontinued w.e.f.
31.12.2018. On this basis, it is submitted that
cheque-book was issued to the revisionist in the
year 2008 and as per the RBI circular direction, it
was not effective w.e.f. 31.12.2018; that thus
there was no legal enforceable debt as the cheque
could not have been encashed; that the RBI in its
circular itself has mentioned that the CTS
cheques shall be cleared and will be valid only till
31.12.2018. On this basis, it is submitted that
the alleged cheque was presented for encashment
before the Bank in the year 2022, which could
not have legal enforceable debt. It is further
submitted that the revisionist is ready to furnish
the adequate sureties to the satisfaction of the
court concerned.
11. Learned State Counsel, on the other hand,
vehemently opposed the bail application.
12. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.
13. Having considered the aforesaid
submissions under the facts and circumstances
of the case and also considering the circular
issued by the RBI in which CTS cheques were

discontinued w.e.f. 31.12.2018 and as such the
alleged cheque was presented for encashment
before the Bank in the year 2022, this Court is of
the view that it is a case in which the execution of
sentence should be suspended and the revisionist
be enlarged on bail.
14. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.
15. Let the revisionist/applicant be released on
bail, during the pendency of the instant criminal
revision, on furnishing personal bonds and two
reliable sureties each of the like amount to the
satisfaction of the court concerned. Execution of
sentence and realisation of fine shall also remain
suspended.
 (Alok Mahra J.)
 03.08.2026
Ujjwal
